summary: Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Eugène Burnouf around 1838–1840 and Christian Lassen around 1840–1841. He was appointed professor at KU Leuven in 1841.
G. V. Aston is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. Between 1986 and 2004, Aston studied under Paul Harrison at the University of Canterbury, earning a Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy.

G. V. Devasthali was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at H.P.T. Arts and R.Y.K. Science College (~1937–1967) and professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University until 1968.

Gadjin Nagao was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at Kyoto University and under Susumu Yamaguchi and Ryotai Hatai. He held the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971), alongside other academic posts.

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She completed her studies at the University of Chicago around 1987 under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, committee member Frank E. Reynolds, and traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as a sub-editor in the Dictionary Department, as well as at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Gananath Obeyesekere was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Washington (~1958–1964). He held posts at the University of California, San Diego (~1972–1980), and Princeton University (~1980–2000).

Ganganatha Jha was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Queen's College and the universities of Calcutta and Allahabad. His career included posts at Darbhanga Raj Library, Muir Central College, and the University of Allahabad, where he served as Vice-Chancellor (~1923–1932).

Gangs zhun is a Tibetology scholar who studied at Hainan College for Nationalities until 1989. Gangs zhun subsequently earned a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Davaa-Ochir studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa and earned an M. Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo (~2006–2008) under supervisor Hanna Havnevik.

Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Jean-Daniel Kieffer and at Lycée Thiers. From around 1828 to 1878, he held posts at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and INALCO as professor of Hindustani.

Gareth Fisher is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After earning a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology at the University of Virginia (~2000–2006), Fisher became Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University around 2011.

Gareth Sparham is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and the University of British Columbia, later holding posts at UBC and the University of Michigan.

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1973–1979). He served on the faculty at Harvard University (~1979–1985), Columbia University (~1999–2007), and joined the University of Chicago around 2007.

Gary D. DeAngelis is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied under mentors Masatoshi Nagatomi and William J. Johnson. He has served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross.
Gary Goh is a scholar in the field of philosophy. Goh's academic training includes studying under teacher Brook Ziporyn and under Jay L. Garfield as foster supervisor.

Gary Snyder is a scholar of Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley. He held academic posts at the University of California, Irvine, and the University of California, Davis (~1986).

Gary Urton is a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He held posts at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (2002–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1834. He later served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Turin (~1852–1891) and as librarian at the Royal Library of Turin (~1859–1891).

Gavin D'Costa is a scholar of religious studies who was educated at Bedford Modern School and the University of Birmingham (~1980–1983). Around 1993, he took up a post as Professor in Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol.
